Text and image to video with Wan 2.2: 5 second clips at 832x480 or 1280x704. Slower than Neodragon and much better. 6.25 GB: the Wan 2.2 Turbo DiT, its umT5 text encoder and a small decoder.

Image to video with Wan 2.2 14B: your picture moving, with the motion and detail of the 14B. Wire a picture into a Wan 2.2 14B node, or use the Text to video (14B) flow. About 9 minutes for 2 seconds at 480x832 and 12 minutes for 1 second at 720x1280 on an 8 Elite; faces come out much sharper at the larger size. 8 Elite or newer, 12 GB phones and up. About 21 GB (two 8.6 GB models with the 4-step speed-up built in); with Wan 2.2 Turbo installed its text encoder is shared. Use Wi-Fi.

About 4.3 GB each, and ~9 GB free while it unpacks. Slow: about 80 s a picture. Close other apps while it renders. Use Wi-Fi.

Klein 4B about 6.7 GB, Klein 9B about 10.7 GB and slower. 8 Gen 3 or newer (alpha on 8 Gen 3, where Klein 4B is a 6.9 GB GGUF); Klein 9B also runs on 8 Gen 2 (alpha). Any size from 512 to 2048. Use Wi-Fi.
About 8.8 GB on an 8 Elite or newer; a smaller Q4_0 build on 8 Gen 3 and 8 Gen 2 (alpha). Still maturing: it crashes on some 8 Elite phones. Use Wi-Fi.
About 10.8 GB. 8 Gen 3 or newer (alpha on 8 Gen 3). Edits and generates; slower than FLUX.2. Use Wi-Fi.
About 9.5 GB. 12 GB phones and up, 8 Gen 3 or newer (alpha on 8 Gen 3). On a 12 GB phone it renders in parts: about 3.5 to 4 minutes at 1024x1024. Text to image only; it does not edit. Use Wi-Fi.

About 3.2 GB. Downloads Anima\'s official 4.2 GB file and converts it on the phone, so it needs ~7.5 GB free while it installs. About 1 minute a picture at 1024², any size from 512. 8 Gen 1 or newer (alpha on 8 Gen 1, 8 Gen 2 and 8 Gen 3; on the 8 Gen 1 several minutes a picture). Not an edit model. Use Wi-Fi.

About 5.8 GB. Downloads the official 6 GB file from speridlabs and converts it on the phone, so it needs ~10 GB free while it installs. About 2.5 minutes a picture at 1024x1024 on an 8 Elite. No VAE. Only the sizes it was trained at (about 1 MP each). 8 Gen 2 or newer (alpha below the 8 Elite, not yet run on a real 8 Gen 2 or 8 Gen 3). Text to image only. Use Wi-Fi.

About 10 GB. 8 Gen 3 or newer (alpha on 8 Gen 3). A careful, detailed picture model with an 8-step speed-up applied every time. About 50 seconds at 512x512 and under 3 minutes at 1024x1024 on an 8 Elite. Text to image only. Use Wi-Fi.

About 11.6 GB. 12 GB phones and up, 8 Elite or newer. Best at readable text in a picture: signs, posters, labels. An 8-step speed-up applied every time. About 5.5 minutes at 768x768 on an 8 Elite. Text to image only. Non-commercial use only (Ideogram\'s licence). Use Wi-Fi.

About 6.2 GB. 8 Elite or newer. The newest picture model from Black Forest Labs: sharp detail and good prompt following, 16 steps. About 45 seconds at 512x512 and 2 minutes at 1024x1024 on an 8 Elite. Text to image only. Under the FLUX Kommunity License. Use Wi-Fi.
About 3.5 GB each, and ~7.5 GB free while it unpacks. Use Wi-Fi.

FLUX.2 Klein or Qwen Image 2.1, on an 8 Gen 3 or newer (alpha on 8 Gen 3). A photo and a prompt: the whole picture is re-rendered to follow it, rather than nudged. Wire a second picture into the reference port and name them as image 1 and image 2 in the prompt.
A prompt into a clip. Wan 2.2 Turbo by default (minutes, much better); switch the video node to Neodragon for 2 s in about 30 s.
Your picture model makes the first frame from the prompt, then Wan 2.2 14B animates it: the best motion and detail, and slow. Check the picture first: a new one takes seconds, a new clip minutes.
A picture as the first frame of a clip, moving the way the prompt says. Wan 2.2 Turbo by default; Neodragon on the video node for speed.
Clip length in seconds, 24 frames each; 0 makes one still picture. 5 s at 480p takes about 3 minutes on an 8 Elite.

Recommended: 1280x704 or 704x1280, the size Wan 2.2 is made for. 832x480 or 480x832 is about three times faster but can look soft or distorted. Any shape up to 1280x704 worth of pixels; the other side shrinks when you pass it.

Recommended: 1280x720 or 720x1280 for faces and fine detail (about 12 minutes for 1 second on an 8 Elite). 832x480 or 480x832 to try an idea first (about 5 minutes for 1 second), but faces come out soft. Any shape up to 1280x720 worth of pixels; the other side shrinks when you pass it.
